messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: 25OHD levels did not differ significantly between patients treated for depression and healthy controls.
Sentence: "The level of 25OHD and 1,25(OH)2D3 did not differ significantly between the examined groups."
Measured as: depression (patients treated for depression vs healthy controls)
Population: 99 patients aged 46.9 ± 11 years treated for depression and 45 healthy subjects
Intervention: Not applicable (observational; serum 25OHD measured)
Comparator: Healthy controls
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 144
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Serum 25(OH)D of 20 ng/mL or lower independently predicted depressive symptoms (CES-D score of 16 or higher) in sarcoidosis patients.
Sentence: "In a multivariate binomial logistic regression model, the following independent predictors of CES-D score ≥16 were identified: female gender (odds ratio, OR 1.983), chronic sarcoidosis (OR 2.311), serum levels of 25(OH)D ≤20 ng/mL (OR 2.326), persistent dry cough (OR 2.173), FAS Scores ≥22 (OR 9.243), and chest X-ray stage 3 (8.851)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (CES-D score ≥16)
Population: 400 sarcoidosis patients in a cross-sectional study
Intervention: serum 25(OH)D ≤20 ng/mL (measured level, not administered)
Comparator: serum 25(OH)D above 20 ng/mL
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 400
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed
